speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me when these skin lesions first appeared and if they are itchy or painful?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the exposure to chickenpox and the up-to-date immunization status, these painless papules are likely molluscum contagiosum. Do the lesions have a central dimple or umbilication, and are there any signs of secondary bacterial infection like pus or crusting?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical presentation of skin-colored, pearly papules with central umbilication is pathognomonic for molluscum contagiosum. DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum contagiosum
